title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
keyIdea: The next unused preorder value is the root of the current range. Its position in inorder (from a value → index map) splits the range: left part builds the left subtree, right part the right subtree. Recurse left first with a shared preIndex.

approaches.name: Search the root in inorder each time
approaches.idea: Same recursion, but find the root's position by scanning the inorder range.
approaches.why: Up to O(n) scan for each of n nodes (e.g. a chain).

approaches.name: Value → index map + recursion
approaches.idea: Map each inorder value to its index. solve(start, end): root = preorder[preIndex++], split at map[root], build left then right.
approaches.why: Each node is created once with an O(1) lookup; map O(n), recursion O(h).

quiz.q: Why is preorder[preIndex] the root of the current range?
options: Preorder lists every root before its subtrees, and ranges are built in that same order

quiz.q: What does the root's position in inorder tell you?
options: Everything left of it in the range is the left subtree; everything right is the right subtree

quiz.q: Why build the left subtree before the right?
options: Preorder is root, left, right, so preIndex reaches the left subtree's values first
Because inorder goes left first only

quiz.q: Why does this need unique values?
options: The map must give one position per value to split the range
